defendant: LINCOLN ELECTRIC AUTOMATION, INC. (F/K/A WAYNE TRAIL TECHNOLOGIES, INC.), 407 South Main Street, Fort Laramie, OH 45845. An Ohio corporation. Name changed from Wayne Trail Technologies, Inc. by Certificate of Amendment filed with the Ohio Secretary of State on 2020-12-18. No attorney ever appeared.
agreement: Grant Agreement. The complaint calls it a Grant Agreement throughout, with JobsOhio as Grantor and the defendant as Grantee, and pleads that JobsOhio 'agreed to provide Defendant $100,000.00 in grant funds conditioned on Defendant complying with all terms of the Grant Agreement.'
program: Not named. The complaint describes JobsOhio's mission and 'the use of strategic grants and project funding' but never names one of JobsOhio's published incentive programs.
amount_sought: $100,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees, costs and expenses. This is the full grant amount disbursed.
job_commitments: From paragraph 4: create 50 new jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $3,750,000.00; retain 170 existing jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $13,000,000.00; and make a total fixed asset investment at the Project Site of $6,800,000.00. Project Site is both 407 South Main Street and 203 East Park Street, Fort Laramie, OH 45845. Metric Evaluation Date 2019-12-31; metrics to be maintained through the Metric Expiration Date of 2021-12-31.
shortfall: From paragraph 10: the defendant's own 2021 Annual Report 'acknowledged that Defendant failed to satisfy its Metric Commitments.' It 'only created 13 new jobs, with an associated payroll of $817,938.21' against a requirement of 50 new jobs and $3,750,000.00 of payroll, and 'further failed to make total fixed asset investments in the amount of $6,800,000.00.' The complaint does not state what fixed asset investment was actually made. JobsOhio issued a demand letter dated 2022-08-10 (Exhibit 3) demanding repayment of the $100,000.00; the defendant 'refused and/or failed to return the grant funds.'
repayment_quote: Section 5, quoted at paragraph 5: '5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under section 9 of this Agreement. *** (Emphasis added).' ||| Section 6(b), quoted at paragraph 6: '(b) Annual Reports. Grantee shall submit to Grantor an annual report in the format required by Grantor (the "Annual Report"). Each Annual Report shall provide information for the applicable reporting period detailing the progress of the Project, and Metric Commitments to date. Annual Reports shall be submitted by Grantee for each calendar year (or part of a year) during the Term of this Agreement, and each Annual Report shall be received by Grantor no later than March 1 following the calendar year covered by such Annual Report. Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9. (Emphasis added).' ||| Section 9(b), quoted at paragraph 7: '(b) Remedies. Following a default by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. Grantor may demand repayment of all or a portion of Grant Funds disbursed. Grantee shall repay such Grant Funds within thirty (30) days after written demand by Grantor. (Emphasis added). (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law.' ||| The complaint also pleads at paragraph 10 (the second paragraph numbered 10) that 'Pursuant to Section 9(e) of the Grant Agreement, Defendant is further liable for JobsOhio's attorney fees, costs, and expenses incurred in bringing this action,' but does not quote Section 9(e).
remedy_named: Repayment. Section 9(b)(ii) is headed 'Demand Repayment of Grant Funds.' The words clawback and liquidated damages do not appear. This differs from the Olive AI Talent Acquisition Services Agreement, whose Section 9(b)(ii) is headed 'Liquidated Damages.' The section numbering, 5 for metrics and 9(b) for remedies, is parallel but not identical.
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. Paragraph 4 says the Grant Agreement is 'attached hereto as Exhibit 2.' The complaint PDF is 29 pages: a 4-page complaint followed by Exhibit 1 (the Ohio Secretary of State Certificate of Amendment), Exhibit 2 (the Grant Agreement itself) and Exhibit 3 (the 2022-08-10 demand letter). This is the opposite of the Olive AI case, where JobsOhio refused to attach the agreement on confidentiality and trade-secret grounds. The exhibit pages were retrieved but their full text was not transcribed.
outcome: Dismissed by JobsOhio without prejudice, before any answer was filed. The filing is captioned 'PLAINTIFF JOBSOHIO'S NOTICE OF DISMISSAL WITHOUT PREJUDICE' and reads in full: 'Now comes the Plaintiff JobsOhio ("JobsOhio') and hereby dismisses this case without prejudice.' No judgment was ever entered. The defendant never appeared or answered; JobsOhio filed four consecutive consents to move or plead between 2022-10-20 and 2022-12-21, which is consistent with negotiation, but no settlement agreement, judgment entry or dismissal entry stating terms is in the file.
amount_recovered: Not stated anywhere in the record. No judgment was entered, no satisfaction of judgment was filed, and the dismissal notice states no terms. Nothing in the file establishes that JobsOhio received any money.

notes: This is the clearest public statement of a JobsOhio cash grant agreement's repayment terms found in this batch, and unlike the Olive AI case the agreement itself is attached to the complaint. Counsel is the same firm as in the Olive AI suit, Mann & Carducci Co. LPA (Robert J. Mann, Mary Spahia-Carducci). notes: The most important mechanic in this complaint is the escalation. JobsOhio first demanded a partial repayment of $68,000.00 against a $125,000.00 grant, and when the company did not pay within the 30 days Section 9(b)(ii) allows, JobsOhio sued for the full $125,000.00. The complaint treats the missed 30-day deadline as a separate breach that unlocks the whole grant. The input file records $525,000 paid to United Candle Company LLC across 2021 and 2022, while this suit concerns a single $125,000 grant agreement dated 2019-07-29; the record does not reconcile the two figures. Counsel is Mann & Carducci Co. LPA, the same firm as in the Lincoln Electric and Olive AI suits, and the quoted sections are near-identical across them, which suggests a standard JobsOhio grant agreement form.

defendant: TOWER AUTOMOTIVE OPERATIONS USA I, LLC. Project site 630 Southwest Street, Bellevue, OH 44811. Judge Chris M. Brown. The company appeared through David A. Lockshaw Jr. of Dickinson Wright PLLC on 2021-10-22.
agreement: Grant Agreement. JobsOhio 'provided Defendant $250,000.00 in grant funds conditioned on Defendant achieving all metrics set forth in the Grant Agreement.'
program: Not named. The complaint never names one of JobsOhio's published incentive programs, although the metrics include a training investment, which is a feature of workforce programs.
amount_sought: $250,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees and costs. This is the full grant.
job_commitments: From paragraph 4, the largest set of commitments in this batch: create 138 new jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $5,979,000.00; train 138 employees with a training investment of $2,500,000.00; retain 82 jobs with a payroll of at least $3,546,000.00; and make fixed asset investments totaling $32,000,000.00. Metric Evaluation Date 2018-12-31; metrics to be maintained through the Metric Expiration Date of 2020-12-31.
shortfall: No shortfall is established. This complaint is a reporting-default case. Paragraph 8 pleads that the defendant 'breached the Grant Agreement by, among other matters, failing to timely file Annual Reports showing it has satisfied its Metric Commitments as required under Section 6(b) of the Grant Agreement,' that JobsOhio 'declared the Grant Agreement to be in breach pursuant to a letter dated July 20, 2021, (See Exhibit 2), and demanded repayment of the $250,000.00 grant,' and only then adds, 'Based upon information and belief, Defendant is further in default for failing to satisfy its Metric Commitments.' No job, payroll or investment figure actually achieved is pleaded anywhere in the complaint.
repayment_quote: Section 5, quoted at paragraph 5: '5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. *** (a) Metric Commitment. Grantee must attain all Metric Commitments set forth on the first page of this Agreement no later than the Metric Evaluation Date, unless otherwise changed in accordance with this Agreement. Once Metric Commitments have been met, Grantee shall maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. *** (c) Remedy. If Grantee fails to satisfy its obligations under Section 5(a), Section 6(b), or to maintain substantial operations at the Project site during the Term, Grantee is in default of this Agreement and Grantor may seek the remedies provided to Grantor under section 9 of this Agreement. *** (Emphasis added).' This 2015 version of Section 5(a) adds the words 'unless otherwise changed in accordance with this Agreement,' which the 2017 and 2019 versions quoted in 22CV006725 and 25CV009066 do not contain. ||| Section 6(b) is quoted only in fragment at paragraph 6: 'Failure by Grantee to submit any Annual Report shall be a default for which Grantor may terminate this Agreement as set forth in Section 9.' ||| Section 9(b), quoted at paragraph 7: '(b) Remedies: Following a default by Grantee, Grantor may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Demand Repayment of Grant Funds. The notice reads in full: 'Now comes Plaintiff JobsOhio and hereby dismisses this case without prejudice.' No judgment was entered.
amount_recovered: Not stated anywhere in the record. No judgment, no satisfaction, no settlement terms in the file. notes: This is the clearest example in the batch of JobsOhio suing for the whole grant over paperwork. The pleaded breach is the failure to file Annual Reports, not any proven shortfall; the metric failure is pleaded only 'upon information and belief.' defendant: CANDID CARE CO. Project site 34 South Third Street, Fifth Floor, Columbus, Ohio 43215. Judge Jeffrey M. Brown. The company was represented by Todd Seaman of Thompson Hine LLP.
agreement: Talent Acquisition Services Agreement (TAS Agreement). NOT a grant agreement. JobsOhio did not hand money to the company. Paragraph 4 explains the mechanism: 'JobsOhio utilizes subcontractors for performance of the talent acquisition services, with JobsOhio agreeing to fund such services up to a specified amount, and the company agreeing to repay JobsOhio the cost of such services should the company fail to fulfill, as applicable, its fixed asset investment, job creation, job retention, job training, and payroll and training cost commitments.' The services include 'providing data that can be used to assist a company in selecting and enhancing its overall candidate attraction strategies related to pre-selected job postings and media channels, increasing the volume of candidates applying to open positions at the company through a variety of job posting and advertising strategies, and increasing community awareness of companies and their role as an employer in the local area.' JobsOhio agreed to provide services 'up to the amount of $200,000.00' and pleads it 'incurred $200,000.00 in subcontractor costs.'
agreement_date: On or about 2019-01-23, with four amendments dated 2019-02-05, 2020-05-21, 2020-09-24 and 2021-06-05, all collectively called the TAS Agreement.
program: Not named. Paragraph 4 calls it 'one of its incentive offerings' and never names one of JobsOhio's published programs. This is the same phrase used in the Olive AI complaint.
amount_sought: $200,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, costs, expenses and reasonable attorney fees. This is the full service value, not the $18,000.00 JobsOhio had demanded before suit.
job_commitments: From paragraph 6: create 150 new jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $6,000,000.00, and make total fixed asset investments at the Project Site of $850,000.00. Metric Evaluation Date 2021-12-31; metrics to be maintained through the Metric Expiration Date of 2023-12-31. No job retention commitment is pleaded.
shortfall: From paragraph 11: per the defendant's own 2023 Annual Report, it 'only created 57 new jobs at the Project Site, instead of the required 150 new jobs, and the new jobs had an associated payroll of $3,520,695, instead of the required payroll of at least $6,000,000.00.' The complaint does not say whether the $850,000.00 fixed asset investment was made.
repayment_quote: Section 2(b), quoted at paragraph 7: 'Obligations of Company. JobsOhio has approved provision of the Deliverables and Services to the Company to induce Company to undertake and complete the Project, with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans at the Project Address above. Accordingly, the Company's completion of the Project, maintaining operations at the Project Address during the Term, and achieving at the Project Address Company's Metric Commitment obligations set forth on the first page of this Agreement ("Metric Commitments"), are each essential terms of this Agreement. Company hereby agrees that it: (i) Must attain all Metric Commitments no later than the Metric Evaluation Date, and once met, must maintain such Metric Commitments through the Metric Expiration Date. (Emphasis added).' ||| Section 9(b), quoted at paragraph 9: '*** In the event of a Breach by Company, JobsOhio may terminate this Agreement and may in addition exercise one or more of the following remedies: *** (ii) Liquidated Damages. As liquidated damages, Company shall pay JobsOhio upon demand the value of each category of Service and/or Deliverable listed on the Talent Acquisition Services Project Budget in Exhibit A that has been performed, whether or not completed, at the time of the Breach; or (iii) Other Legal Remedies. Pursue any other legal or equitable remedies Grantor may have under this Agreement or applicable law. (Emphasis added).' The word 'Grantor' in clause (iii) appears in the quoted text even though this agreement has no Grantor, which suggests the TAS form was adapted from the grant agreement form. ||| Section 9(a)(ii) is paraphrased, not quoted, at paragraph 8: it 'provides that Defendant is in breach of the TAS Agreement if Defendant fails to comply with the Metric Commitments.' ||| Section 9(g) is paraphrased, not quoted, at paragraph 14: it 'provides that in the event an action is filed to enforce the TAS Agreement, the prevailing party is entitled to recover all costs and expenses, including reasonable attorney fees, from the non-prevailing party.'
remedy_named: Liquidated Damages. Section 9(b)(ii) is headed 'Liquidated Damages,' the same heading as in the Olive AI TAS Agreement and different from the 'Demand Repayment of Grant Funds' heading in the cash grant agreements. The schedule of values is here called the 'Talent Acquisition Services Project Budget in Exhibit A,' whereas the Olive AI agreement called it the 'Talent Acquisition Services Value Allocation in Exhibit A.'
agreement_is_exhibit: No, and the complaint gives its reason at paragraph 6: 'A copy of the TAS Agreement is not attached as it contains confidential and/or competitive and/or trade secret information, and as it further contains confidentiality provisions, and Defendant already has a copy in its possession.' This is the Olive AI language with an extra clause added, 'and as it further contains confidentiality provisions.' The 6-page complaint PDF is a 5-page complaint plus Exhibit 1, the 2025-02-14 demand letter.
outcome: Dismissed by JobsOhio WITH prejudice, 57 days after filing. The notice reads in full: 'Now comes Plaintiff JobsOhio and hereby dismisses this action with prejudice.' It was served on the company's counsel at Thompson Hine LLP. Certified mail service had failed on 2025-11-25, so the company apparently learned of the suit another way and engaged counsel. No answer was filed and no judgment was entered.
amount_recovered: Not stated anywhere in the record. A dismissal with prejudice bars JobsOhio from refiling, which is the usual signature of a settled case, but no settlement agreement, judgment or payment figure is in the file, and nothing establishes that any money changed hands.

defendant: KEYSTONE TAILORED MANUFACTURING, LLC, 4600 Tiedeman Rd., Brooklyn, OH 44144. An Ohio limited liability company. Judge Mark A. Serrott. The company appeared and fought, through James M. Drozdowski of Kaufman, Drozdowski & Grendell, LLC.
agreement: Grant Agreement. JobsOhio 'provided Defendant $420,000.00 in grant funds conditioned on Defendant achieving all metrics set forth in the Grant Agreement.'
program: Not named. The complaint never names one of JobsOhio's published incentive programs.
amount_sought: $420,000.00, plus interest including prejudgment interest, reasonable attorney fees and costs. This is the full grant.
job_commitments: From paragraph 4: invest $6 million in fixed assets at the Project Site; create 20 new jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $600,000.00; and retain 150 total jobs at the Project Site with a payroll of at least $4.6 million. Metric Evaluation Date 2018-12-31; metrics to be maintained through the Metric Expiration Date of 2020-12-31.
shortfall: No metric figure is pleaded. The breach alleged is the plant closing itself. Paragraph 6: 'On January 10, 2019, Defendant sent a "Warn Notice of Plant Closing" to the Ohio Department of Jobs & Family Services advising that it would be permanently closing its plant at the Project Site no later than March 11, 2019, pursuant to which it would be laying off the majority of its employees as of such time, with a "few" employees remaining to finish the plant closing.' Paragraph 7 notes the closing comes 'only a few months after the Metric Evaluation Date of December 31, 2018' and 'more than a year and half before the Metric Expiration Date.' JobsOhio sent a default letter on 2019-01-29 demanding repayment of the full $420,000.00, and 'Defendant has refused to repay the grant funds.'
repayment_quote: Only Section 5 is quoted. From paragraph 5: '5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement.' This 2015 complaint calls it 'paragraph 5' of the Grant Agreement rather than Section 5, and it quotes no subsection (a) or (c). Section 6 and Section 9 are not quoted anywhere in this complaint, and no repayment or remedy provision is set out in the agreement's own words. The complaint instead pleads a common-law theory, Count I being 'Breach of Grant Agreement/Anticipatory Breach/Repudiation.' This is the earliest complaint in the batch and the least complete in its quotation of the agreement; the later complaints by the same firm quote Sections 5(a), 5(c), 6(b) and 9(b) in full.
remedy_named: None named in the quoted text, because the remedies section is not quoted. The theory pleaded is anticipatory breach and repudiation at common law, with the remedy sought being repayment of the full grant. The words clawback and liquidated damages do not appear.
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. Paragraph 4 says the Grant Agreement is 'attached hereto as Exhibit 1.' outcome: Settled, with the settlement figure stated on the record, then dismissed with prejudice. This is the only case in the batch where a dollar amount of settlement appears in a filing. amount_recovered: Not determinable from the record. shortfall: No shortfall figure is pleaded. This is a reporting-default case, like the Tower Automotive suit. Paragraph 7: the defendant 'breached the Grant Agreement by, among other matters, failing to timely file annual reports showing it has satisfied its metric obligations as required under Section 6(b) of the Grant Agreement. As a result, JobsOhio declared the Grant Agreement to be in breach pursuant to a letter dated June 2, 2020, (See Exhibit 3), and demanded repayment of the $70,000.00 grant in accordance with the terms of the Grant Agreement. Based upon information and belief, Defendant is further in default for failing to satisfy its metric obligations.' The complaint adds a sentence found nowhere else in the batch: 'Defendant's noncompliance predated, and was neither caused by nor related to, the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.'
repayment_quote: Only the preamble of Section 5 is quoted. From paragraph 6: '5. Metrics and Maintenance of Operations. Grantor has approved an award of financial assistance to Grantee to induce Grantee to undertake and complete the Project with the goal of attracting and retaining business opportunities for the State of Ohio that create and/or retain a significant number of jobs for Ohioans. Accordingly, achieving Grantee's Metric Commitment obligations at the Project site during the Term are essential terms of this Agreement. (Emphasis added).' Section 5(a), Section 5(c), Section 6(b) and Section 9 are referred to but not quoted. Section 6(b) is cited at paragraph 7 as the annual report obligation, and the attorney-fee entitlement is pleaded as resting on 'the terms of the Grant Agreement' without a section number. This is one of two complaints in the batch, with 19CV001481, that never sets out the remedies clause in the agreement's own words.
remedy_named: None named in the quoted text, because the remedies clause is not quoted. The complaint pleads only that JobsOhio 'demanded repayment of the $70,000.00 grant in accordance with the terms of the Grant Agreement.' Neither clawback nor liquidated damages appears.
agreement_is_exhibit: Yes. Paragraph 4 says the Grant Agreement is 'attached hereto as Exhibit 1' and paragraph 5 attaches the Amendment as Exhibit 2. The 15-page complaint PDF is a 3-page complaint plus Exhibit 1 (the Grant Agreement), Exhibit 2 (the 2018 Amendment) and Exhibit 3 (the breach letter of 2020-06-02). The exhibit pages were retrieved but not transcribed.
outcome: Agreed judgment for the full amount with a payment schedule, and a summary judgment entry four days later for the same amount. The company answered out of rule on 2020-08-25 with leave granted on 2020-08-26. JobsOhio moved for summary judgment on 2020-09-08 with a 158-page exhibit set; the company responded on 2020-10-05. On 2020-10-22 Judge McIntosh signed an Agreed Judgment Entry: 'Judgment is hereby entered for Plaintiff JobsOhio and against Defendant E1 Digital Direct, Inc. in the amount of $70,000.00. Defendant shall pay the foregoing judgment amount as follows: 1. Defendant shall pay Plaintiff $10,000.00 on or before October 25, 2020. 2. Defendant shall pay the remaining balance in 12 equal installments of $5,000.00 each, with the first installment due on or before November 25, 2020, and the subsequent installments due on or before the 25th day of each month thereafter, until the entire $70,000.00 judgment has been paid in full. Defendant shall further be responsible for all court costs herein.' The case was terminated the same day and the summary judgment motion marked moot. On 2020-10-26 the court nonetheless signed a separate Judgment Entry granting the summary judgment motion and entering judgment 'for Plaintiff and against Defendant in the amount of $70,000.00, plus reasonable attorney fees and costs as provided under the terms of the Grant Agreement,' with a 7-day and 14-day procedure for fixing the fee amount.
outcome_date: 2020-10-22 for the agreed judgment; 2020-10-26 for the summary judgment entry.
amount_recovered: Not stated. The agreed judgment set out a 13-payment schedule totaling $70,000.00 ending around 2021-10-25, but no satisfaction of judgment was filed and no later docket entry records any payment. The schedule is what the parties agreed would be paid, not evidence of what was paid. Nothing in the record establishes any recovery. No attorney fee amount was ever fixed on the docket.

notes: The second reporting-default case in the batch, and the second where the complaint never quotes the remedies clause. JobsOhio demanded the entire $70,000.00 because annual reports were not filed, pleaded the metric failure only 'upon information and belief,' and got the full amount. The complaint goes out of its way to foreclose a pandemic defense, which no other complaint in the batch does. Note the two judgment entries four days apart for the same $70,000.00: a negotiated installment judgment on 2020-10-22 that terminated the case, then a summary judgment entry on 2020-10-26 that also adds attorney fees. The record does not explain the sequence. The input file shows $0 paid to E1 Digital Direct on the Form 990 grant schedule across 2019 and 2020, while the complaint pleads $70,000.00 disbursed under a 2016 agreement; the record does not reconcile the two, and the grant predates the Schedule I years shown.
